title: Orient to reference
tagline: Flip surfaces so their normals point toward -- or away from -- a reference, so every feature downstream that follows the normal keeps working whatever happens upstream.

slides.title: What it does
slides.problem: Many features pick their side by a surface's normal: Thicken's Thickness 1, Offset surface, extrude 'up to', Move face, Split front / back. Normals flip freely when an upstream loft, offset, mirror or sketch changes -- and the reference-side features keep their inputs' orientation. Orient to reference fixes the normal itself: each surface is turned to face the reference (or away).
useWhen: A built-in downstream follows a surface's normal
Surfaces come from different sources and face different ways
You want to SEE which way a set of surfaces faces (normal arrows)
slides.caption: A flip names a side relative to a normal; a reference names it in the model.

points.head: Per surface body
points.body: s = (P - C) . n at the body's point nearest the reference. s > 0: the normal already points toward it.

points.head: Flip only what is wrong
points.body: Bodies facing the wrong way are flipped (opFlipOrientation); the rest are left exactly as they are.

points.head: Surfaces only
points.body: Solids always face outward and cannot be flipped; selecting one is an error.

slides.title: The dialog
params: Surface bodies, or faces of them (a face orients its whole surface body).
Geometry on the side the normals should face: best a mate connector or vertex near the surfaces.
The arrow. On: every normal points toward the reference. Off: away from it.
While editing: arrows along each face's normal, after orientation. Green = already right, orange = flipped here.
Print sides: each surface's distance to the reference and whether it was flipped.

slides.title: Examples: the normals, evaluated
slides.head: Test geometry R1-R3, normals read back from Onshape after the feature ran
slides.body: Two sheets with opposite normals and a reference between them: 'toward' leaves both alone because they already face it (green); 'away' flips both (orange). A half cylinder with the reference on its axis: every normal ends up pointing at the axis.

keys: The surfaces that already faced the right way.
messages: Flipped N of M surface(s); K already faced toward / away from the reference.
A solid's faces cannot be flipped
Select surfaces; solids always face outward.
The reference lies on surface k
Move the reference clearly off that surface.

items.head: Put it right before the built-in
items.body: Orient the surfaces just before the Thicken, Offset surface or extrude that follows their normal.

items.head: Use a local reference
items.body: A mate connector or vertex near the surfaces, on the side meant. A far plane can read the wrong side where a surface curves.

items.head: Or skip the built-in
items.body: Thicken+ and Offset+ read the side from a reference directly and do not care which way the normal points.

items.head: One orientation per body
items.body: A merged surface (e.g. a Mutual Trim+ result) is one body and gets one orientation for all its faces.

rows: Split+, Mutual Trim+, Offset+, Thicken+ (same reference rule)
